candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS LHV Group reported a net profit of EUR 24.7 million for the second quarter of 2026, representing a 25% increase from EUR 19.7 million in the first quarter of 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: However, this figure marks a 20% decline compared to EUR 30.8 million in the same period of the previous year.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Earnings per share stood at EUR 0.07, up from EUR 0.06 in Q1 2026 but down from EUR 0.09 in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: The Group’s consolidated net income, a broader measure of operational performance, reached EUR 79.0 million, reflecting a 7.3% growth from the previous quarter and a 7% increase year-over-year.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: The primary driver of the improved quarterly results was a 5% rise in net interest income to EUR 62.5 million, supported by higher market interest rates and growth in the loan portfolio.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Net interest income grew by 8% compared to Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Conversely, net service fee income remained largely flat at EUR 14.6 million, showing a 6% decrease from the prior year, which the Management Board attributed to lower client activity.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Operating expenses decreased by 4% to EUR 43.6 million in the quarter, though they were 8% higher than in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: The cost-to-income ratio for the quarter was 61.9%, an increase from 53.9% in Q1 2026 and 47.3% in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: A significant factor impacting profitability was the increase in loan and bond provisions, which amounted to EUR 5.8 million in Q2 2026, compared to EUR 1.3 million in Q1 2026 and a reversal of EUR 4.2 million in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The Management Board explained that these charges reflected forward-looking model provisions for specific clients, despite the overall loan portfolio quality remaining strong.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Income tax expenses decreased to EUR 5.0 million from EUR 7.1 million in the previous quarter.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: The Group’s loan volume grew by 3% to EUR 5,768 million by the end of Q2 2026, with a 15% increase compared to Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: This growth was driven by home loans and corporate lending, particularly in the real estate sector.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: In contrast, total customer deposits decreased by 3% to EUR 7,557 million, primarily due to a reduction in platform deposits and deposits from financial intermediaries.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: The return on equity for the quarter was 13.1%, higher than the 10.7% in Q1 2026 but lower than the 17.4% recorded in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Capital adequacy stood at 20.8% at the end of the quarter, down from 21.7% in Q1 2026 and 23.0% in Q2 2025, though it remained above the Group’s internal target of 20.0%.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: During the quarter, the Group implemented strategic changes, including a transition to a cloud-based core system architecture and a shift to a product-based management model.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Additionally, LHV Pank received a crypto-assets service provider license, marking the first such license for a bank in Estonia.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Despite these developments, the Management Board noted that the quarter was slightly weaker than planned, primarily due to higher-than-expected expenses and lower service fee income, although interest income performance exceeded forecasts.
